findings.summary: (Fixed this round, re-confirmed.) Step-failure logging no longer interpolates error.stack/message into a free-text string; now logs a structured {event:'pipeline_step_error', error_code} field plus stackFrames(error) (message line stripped). New log-error.ts (errorCode/stackFrames) is applied consistently across every call site that previously leaked. Adversarial e2e (privacy.e2e.spec.ts:241-267) drives a real fake-Gemini provider error and a real malformed-model-value failure and proves neither reaches the log. Residual, correctly-acknowledged limitation: this is call-site discipline backed by a test, not a structural guarantee — a future call site could still build a content-bearing string directly. nfr-verification.md's NFR-04 row states this scope honestly rather than overclaiming a mechanical filter.

(Fixed this round, re-confirmed.) The TLS claim in §6 is now explicitly gated by a pre-release callout ('chỉ công bố bản này khi máy chủ production đã chỉ nhận HTTPS...'), cross-linked from nfr-verification.md's NFR-03 row. The drift test's line-filter (strips '>'-prefixed lines) keeps this callout out of the in-app screen, verified by reading privacy-policy.test.ts's stripMarkdownChrome.

Unchanged from prior round, not asked for: retention sweep's WHERE/ORDER BY on a computed date expression plus a status NOT IN filter has no supporting index; low risk today (hourly maintenance job) but will full-scan meetings/users as volume grows.

Unchanged from prior round, not asked for: the one retention-notice push is claimed (retention_notified_at set) atomically before the push is attempted; if the Expo push itself throws, the meeting is marked notified and never retried, so a user can have a meeting deleted having never actually received the promised 7-day warning, surfaced only as a log line.

Unchanged from prior round, not asked for: CLI arg (process.argv[2]) is interpolated directly into a raw SQL template string rather than bound as a parameter; not attacker-reachable (local ops tool, developer-supplied arg) but worth binding on principle.
